`fix` (`api`): **Test an AniDB login against the stored password when none was retyped**:

`GET /api/v3/Settings` masks every secret on the way out, so a client that
posts back what it was handed, rather than what the user retyped, sends the mask
to `POST /api/v3/Settings/AniDB/TestLogin`, which used it as the password and
failed the login. The WebUI's AniDB tab does exactly that: it reads `Password`
out of the settings it fetched.

Saving was never affected, since the save path restores a masked secret before
anything reads it. This is the other kind of endpoint: one that uses a secret
without storing it, where there is no document to pair the mask against.

- Added `ConfigurationSecrets.Resolve`, which reads a mask as "the stored one",
  for any endpoint handed a secret it only uses
- Tested an AniDB login with the stored password when the caller sent a mask,
  and rejected the attempt when nothing is stored to test with

`feat` (`plugin`): **Tell each plugin once every plugin has been set up**:

`Setup` runs in load order, and a dependency always loads before the plugins
that depend on it, so a plugin that owns something other plugins contribute
to is set up before any of its contributors. Freezing a registry in its own
`Setup` would freeze it empty.

- Added `IPlugin.Ready()` with an empty default, called once after every
  plugin's `Setup` and before the web host starts
- Called it through `PluginManager.ReadyPlugins`, skipped when a plugin
  already failed to set up
- Recorded a throw the same way as a failed `Setup`: the web host still
  comes up, and the boot stops with the plugin named

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Take the host's startup steps off the plugin-facing interfaces**:

`AddParts` sat on eight service interfaces, and `ScanForPlugins`,
`RegisterPlugins` and `InitPlugins` on `IPluginManager`, though only the host
ever calls them. On the interfaces they read as the way to contribute, and
they were not: seven of the `AddParts` ignore every call after the first, so a
plugin's call did nothing, and `IImageManager.AddParts` replaced its list, so a
plugin's call dropped every resolver the other plugins contributed. Neither
said so.

- Removed `AddParts` from `IConfigurationService`, `IImageManager`,
  `IMetadataService`, `IAiringScheduleService`, `IVideoService`,
  `IVideoReleaseService`, `IVideoHashingService` and
  `IVideoRelocationService`, and `AddTransformParts`/`AddObserverParts` from
  `IVideoStreamPipelineService`
- Removed `ScanForPlugins`, `RegisterPlugins` and `InitPlugins` from
  `IPluginManager`
- Resolved each service through its interface in `PluginManager` and handed it
  its parts only when it is the implementation that takes them, and did the
  same for `RegisterPlugins` in `Startup`, so the registered service types are
  unchanged
- Gave `ImageManager.AddParts` the once-only guard the others have
- Said in the plugin README that implementing a contract is the whole of it

`fix` (`release`): **Enqueue the rescan that `TryScheduleRescanForVideo` builds**:

The method saved a new match attempt and built the provider chain, then
returned `true` without submitting it. `ScanForMissingReleaseInfoJob`
therefore never rescanned anything, and every sweep still inflated the
video's `AttemptCount`.

The chain is submitted with a plain `Enqueue` rather than
`EnqueueAfterCurrent`, since the caller is a recurring sweep over many
videos and each rescan jumping the queue would crowd out everything else.

`fix` (`release`): **Hand `SearchCompleted` the release a queued search found**:

`FinalizeReleaseSearchJob` raised the event without the release, so on the
queued path `ReleaseInfo` was always `null` and every search looked
unmatched to a subscriber, successful or not. The provider jobs have
already saved what they found, so a successful attempt's release is the
video's current one, and that is what is passed now.

- Threw one `AggregateException` naming every failing plugin, instead of the

- Corrected the remark on `SetupPlugins`, which still said it runs after the

`fix` (`config`): **Match masked secrets in lists by a keyed fingerprint instead of `[Key]`**:

two labels collided, and lost the secret when a label changed.

`fix` (`plugin`): **Set a plugin up before the database, and record the failure instead of throwing**:

`SetupPlugins` ran from `LateStart`, which is after the database is opened,
and let the exception reach that handler. Both were wrong. A plugin should
take its services while the rest of the server is still ahead of it, and
throwing out of the start-up path skips the web host and lets the process
die with nothing left running to report why.

The failure is recorded where it happens and the boot is abandoned once the
web host is listening, so the server stays reachable in a state that names
the plugin that stopped it.

- Moved the call to right after `InitPlugins`, before any database work
- Recorded `StartupFailedException` rather than throwing, and returned the
  host once it is up instead of continuing into setup mode or `LateStart`
- Corrected the contract, which said `Setup` runs after the server is up

`fix` (`plugin`): **Make a failed `Setup` fatal once the web host can report it**:

`Setup` ran from `InitPlugins`, which happens before the web host starts and
before the hosted services a plugin registered, and a plugin that threw was
skipped. That skip could not work: services are registered into the container
before initialization and cannot be taken back out of a built one, so a
skipped plugin's hosted services still started. `Shoko.Plugin.Mcp` proved it
by taking the whole server down with a `NullReferenceException` inside
`ConfigurationService.Load`, because the configuration type it reached for
belonged to the plugin that had just been dropped from the exported types.

The fault has to be fatal, then, since it cannot be contained. Running it
late makes it a fatal the operator can read: the web host is already
listening, so `StartupFailedException` reaches the Web UI and names the
plugin instead of the process dying with a stack trace pointing at
configuration.

- Moved the call into `PluginManager.SetupPlugins`, invoked from `LateStart`
  after the session factory is up
- Let the throw reach `LateStart`'s handler, wrapped with the plugin's name
- Dropped the skip, and with it the disposal that only made sense while a
  plugin could be dropped and the server carry on
- Said in the contract that `Setup` runs after the server is up, that
  throwing stops startup, and that the hook only binds on recompile

`feat` (`plugin`): **Let a plugin acquire its services after the container exists**:

A plugin is built twice, and only the second build goes through the
container. Discovery builds it with `Activator.CreateInstance` to read its
identity, which needs a public parameterless constructor and throws without
one, so a plugin that took a constructor dependency never loaded at all and
failed with a `MissingMethodException` that named nothing useful.

`Setup` is the way in instead, mirroring `IQueueJob.Setup`, which exists for
the same reason. The default implementation is a no-op, so nothing already
written has to change.

- Added `IPlugin.Setup(IServiceProvider)` with an empty default
- Called it from `InitPlugins` on the instance the container built
- Skipped a plugin whose `Setup` threw, and disposed it if it can be, rather
  than leaving one loaded that never got what it asked for and would fail
  later somewhere that points nowhere near here

Note that a plugin only gets this on recompile: a `Setup` method compiled
against an abstraction that did not declare one is an ordinary public method
the runtime never maps, so it silently keeps the default. That also means no
existing plugin is hijacked by the new member.

`repo` (`workflows`): **Fail when a plugin download url cannot be resolved**: (_Skip CI_)

Both build workflows resolved a download URL with an unchecked `curl -s`
piped into `jq`, then curled whatever came out. A rate-limited or erroring
API returns a body with no `.assets`, `jq` yields the string `null`, and the
next line fetched that literally: a run failed four seconds in with
`curl: (6) Could not resolve host` while the release it wanted existed and
had its asset attached.

- Resolved with `--fail --silent --show-error`, so an error body never
  reaches `jq`
- Refused an empty or `null` URL with a message naming what could not be
  resolved, rather than passing it to `curl`
- Authenticated the GitHub API call with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so a shared runner
  hitting the unauthenticated rate limit is no longer a build failure
- Downloaded with `--fail`, so a non-2xx response cannot be written into the
  zip and surface later as a corrupt archive

`fix`: **Add missing ISO 639 language mappings and fix subtitle-filename language parsing** ([#1442](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1442)):

* fix(abstractions): add missing ISO 639 language mappings and IETF fallback

`LanguageExtensions.GetTitleLanguage()` was missing 18 codes observed in
production logs (`os`, `ia`, `hz`, `ee`, `ie`, `kr`, `ng`, `enm`, `cu`,
`lg`, `cv`, `an`, `bo`, `io`, `kl`, `li`, `nd`, `ss`), each logged as an
`Unrecognized language string` error every time it was encountered.

Also added a generic fallback for "xxx-XX"-shaped IETF tags (e.g.
`cmn-CN`) that the existing 2-letter+2-letter fast path didn't cover —
strips the country suffix and retries on the language part alone before
reporting unknown.

* fix(core): don't leak garbage text as a language from subtitle filenames

`SubtitleHelper.GetLanguageFromFilename()` only recognized the
`basename.eng.srt` dot-separated convention. Two problems:

- External subtitles named `basename_eng.ass` (underscore, not dot) —
  the actual convention used by some release groups, including
  duplicate-track suffixes like `_eng_1` — weren't recognized at all.
- When a title happened to contain a literal `...` (ellipsis), the dot
  count coincidentally satisfied the "at least 3 dot-parts" check, and
  the unrecognized-segment fallback returned that raw multi-word text
  as if it were a language string, which then got logged repeatedly as
  an unrecognized language.

Added underscore-suffix parsing (with duplicate-track disambiguator
support) tried first, and made the dot-based fallback return null for
segments `GetLanguageFromName` doesn't recognize instead of passing
the raw text through.

NHibernate hands back `DateTimeKind.Unspecified` while the estimator produces

`Unspecified` value treats it as local, shifting the timestamp by the machine's
UTC offset.

  UTC it already is rather than converting it, and routed every airing,
  schedule and channel timestamp through it
- `AiringTrack.Language` carried no `StringEnumConverter` and went over the wire

`fix` (`airing`): **Correct link sets, shared state and trailing estimate shifts**:

Fallout from an adversarial review of the airing schedule service.

- `SetAirings` dissolved a link set of three or more when the head row was
  deleted, unlinking the survivors individually instead of letting
  `NormalizeLinkSets` promote the next smallest member as `RemoveAiring` does
- `LinkAirings` counted its raw argument list, so the same airing passed twice
  produced a self-pointing set of one instead of throwing
- `_airingIDs` was a plain `Dictionary` mutated on queue-worker threads while
  request threads read it, unlike every other shared map on the class
- `_refreshWaiters` never dropped a key, growing one entry per provider and
  entity for the lifetime of the process
- `EstimateAiring` applied `TrailingShiftDays` to every AniDB-anchored estimate,
  shifting gap-fills inside the aired range by a slip that happened later;
  the profile now carries the boundary the shift starts from
- `RefreshAiringScheduleJob` keyed itself on provider and entity id alone,
  because `JobKeyBuilder` rejects enum members unless they are annotated, so a
  refresh for series 5 collided with one for episode 5. It also lacked
  `[DatabaseRequired]` while reading and writing repositories throughout
- A raw `U+0000` byte sat in a string literal in `AiringScheduleUtility`, which
  made the whole file read as binary to grep, diff and friends
- Ten members of `IAiringScheduleService` documented an `InvalidOperationException`
  they never throw, and two throws went undocumented

`feat` (`airing`): **Fire an event when an episode airs**:

that keeps the next hour of airings in memory, so plugins, core and SignalR
clients can react to an episode airing in real time instead of polling
`GetAiringsInRange`.

- `EpisodeAiredEventArgs` carries the enriched airing and the slot that
  passed. It is raised once per **airing**, not per episode: an episode on
  three channels raises it three times, and a consumer that wants "this
  episode aired" de-duplicates by episode itself
- Estimates are raised too, flagged by `IEpisodeAiring.IsEstimated`. An
  estimated event is a prediction, not a fact, and there is no retraction
  event if the estimate later moves; the real airing that follows has its own
  stable ID and raises its own event
- `EpisodeAiringNotificationService` is an `IHostedService` rather than a
  recurring job, because the event has to land within a minute of the slot and
  a queued job waits behind the worker pool and its acquisition filters. It
  wakes every 30 s and works on wall-clock minute boundaries, so it never
  drifts from the minute and never fires early
- The horizon is one hour of airings, rebuilt every 15 minutes and immediately
  on `ScheduleUpdated`, `AiringsUpdated` or `ProvidersUpdated`, so a delay
  reported mid-horizon can't fire at the old time. Estimates are computed
  rather than stored, so filling it runs the read path — which is why it stays
  short
- The "fired through" watermark is a `ScheduledUpdate` row
  (`EpisodeAiringNotifications`). On boot it is moved forward to now and the
  gap is logged rather than replayed: an hours-old prediction is worse than
  none
- Bridged to SignalR as `airing:episode.aired` through a new
  `AiringEventEmitter`, one emitter per service as the rest of the aggregate
  hub does, carrying the same `EpisodeAiring` shape the airings endpoint
  returns
- Documented in the plugin-facing `README.md` and in `AiringSchedule.md`, and
  covered by five tests over the existing airing harness

`refactor` (`airing`): **Replace `EpisodeAired` with a filtered subscription**:

handle. An event could do neither of the two things this needs: carry
per-subscriber filtering, and let the producer do less work.

- Each subscriber brings its own `EpisodeAiringFilteringOptions`, applied
  to its own dispatch. `null` means everything
- `EpisodeAiringNotificationService` builds its horizon from the union of
  the live subscriptions, so `IncludeEstimates` — the expensive flag,
  since estimates run through the read path rather than being stored — is
  only set when a live subscriber wants them

  dispatch at all; only the watermark walks forward. A subscription
  version bump re-arms the horizon on the next tick rather than at the
  next quarter-hour refresh
- Subscriptions live in a `ConcurrentDictionary`; dispose is idempotent
  and thread-safe, and each handler is wrapped so one bad plugin costs
  itself its dispatch and nothing else

`docs` (`streaming`): **Describe what an `IPlaybackObserver` actually observes**:

An observer is called when bytes are served, so what it sees is the sequence of
cache misses, in whatever order the player needed them. The readme presented
the HLS position as precise and the worked example suggested deriving a watched
percentage from it.

- A player requests segments ahead of what it shows, and may request segments it
  never shows
- A seek into cached content produces no request at all, while a seek into
  uncached content does and can be for an earlier point than the last, so the
  reported position jumps both ways
- Progressive playback is weaker again, inferring the position from a byte range
  reaching the end of the file, which does not confirm the bytes reached the
  player

Points at the `/Scrobble` endpoint as the way to get a position the client
vouches for, and drops the same "playback reaches the end" phrasing from the
user data readme.

`feat` (`queue`): **Flow the worker's token to jobs via `IJobCancellationAccessor`**:

`docs` (`actions`): **Follow the token now that the worker supplies one**:

`fix` (`images`): **Accept valid template URLs again**:

broke `PUT /api/v3/Image/Source/{source}` outright and made the

- Dropped the unused `urlErrors` local in `SetTemplateUrlForSource`, left
  over from the validator this predicate was copied from
- Added `ImageTemplateUrlConfigurationTests` covering valid http/https
  template URLs, non-http schemes, relative and malformed URLs, and a
  missing `{0}` placeholder

- Extracted the service's write into `WriteAirings`, shared by

`fix` (`airing`): **Stop de-duplication collapsing separate airings**:

dropped every view `IsSameRelease` matched, and `IsSameRelease` compares

airing of one schedule looked like a copy of the first, so
`GetAiringsForSchedule` answered with one airing however many episodes
the schedule covered, and a channel's own repeat broadcasts of an
episode disappeared from every read.

  collapsed whole schedules against each other rather than single
  airings, so two providers reporting one slot still become one while a
  schedule's own second slot for an episode survives as the rerun it is
- Moved the `PreferredOnly` reduction from "one airing overall" to "one
  airing per episode", and made `GetAiringsInRange` narrow to its window
  before it reduces, so an episode is answered with its best airing in
  the window rather than dropping out of the day it airs on
- Resolved estimates through `GetAiringByID`, which only ever resolved

  handed to clients as an addressable ID

`refactor` (`airing`): **Split the write event into added, updated and withdrawn**:

A write raised one `EpisodeAiringsUpdatedEventArgs` with
`UpdateReason.Updated` carrying every surviving airing, and raised nothing at
all for the rows it deleted, so a consumer could tell neither what was new
nor what had vanished.

- Split the payload into `Added`, `Updated` and `Withdrawn`, leaving
  `Airings` as the three of them in that order
- Called the third one `Withdrawn` because a removal is not always a delete:
  a slot still ahead of us is kept as a slotless hiatus row, and only a slot
  already past is deleted as history
- Kept `Reason` as the one coarse value: `Added`, `Removed` or `None` when
  the write only did that one thing, and `Updated` for everything else
- Carried a hiatus through the inference on `InferredAiring.IsWithdrawn`, so
  a row kept without a slot is reported as a withdrawal rather than as an
  update
- Gave `SetAirings` the skip-if-unchanged treatment `MergeAirings` already
  had, weighing the whole row rather than only what the inference carries, so
  a write that changes nothing moves no `LastUpdatedAt` and reports nothing
- Filled the event the same way from both entry points, so a consumer cannot
  tell which one a provider used

`feat` (`airing`): **Drive provider sweeps from core**:

Added `ISweepingAiringScheduleProvider`, an opt-in sub-interface a provider
implements alongside `IAiringScheduleProvider` to have the server walk its
whole source for it. Core owns enablement, scheduling, pacing and bookkeeping;
the provider owns only the unit of the walk, which genuinely differs per
source.

- `SweepAsync(string?, CancellationToken)` takes the last cursor and answers
  the next one. The cursor is opaque to core, stored capped at 512 characters,
  and `null` means the sweep is finished
- The token is a deadline source linked to the worker's own, so the provider
  observes exactly one token for both the chunk's budget and shutdown. The
  budget is core's, from `AiringScheduleServiceSettings.SweepBudgetSeconds`,
  since a chunk holds a shared queue worker while it runs
- Classified five ways as `AiringScheduleSweepOutcome`: `Completed`,
  `TimedOut`, `Stopped`, `Cancelled` and `Failed`, by asking which source was
  cancelled, which is documented as best effort rather than exact
- `SuggestedSweepInterval` is the provider's declaration and
  `AiringScheduleProviderInfo.SweepInterval` the user's value, the way
  `AvailableKinds` and `EnabledKinds` already pair, clamped to fifteen minutes
  and settable over `/api/v3/AiringSchedule/Provider`
- A chunk that hands back the cursor it was given, or times out without having
  returned one, counts as no progress on `AiringScheduleSweepState`. Three in a
  row holds the sweep back to the provider's interval instead of resuming at
  the next tick, and the log distinguishes too slow from stuck
- `AiringScheduleSweepState` is one row per provider carrying the cursor, the
  last run, the last outcome and that count, with the three-backend schema and
  a migration. No run history: each chunk raises `SweepCompleted` and logs a
  line with the duration, bridged to SignalR as `airing:provider.swept`
- `SweepAiringSchedulesJob` dispatches chunks for the providers that are due,
  and `SweepAiringScheduleProviderJob` runs one chunk for one provider,
  re-queued by the service while the walk keeps moving

`docs` (`airing`): **Document core-driven sweeps**:

Covered the sweep contract for plugin authors and the two provider fields and

- Added `Core-driven sweeps` to the airing README: what a chunk is, what core

- Split `RefreshAsync` from a sweep in the contract bullets, the first being on

`feat` (`queue`): **Let a job declare its own watchdog threshold**:

Added `IJobWatchdogThreshold`, a DI-registered per-job-type threshold the
watchdog asks on every poll, so a job with a deadline longer than
`WatchdogTimeoutSeconds` stays watched instead of reaching for
`[LongRunning]`. Anything the threshold cannot answer with, including a
throw, falls back to the global one, and a type declaring both a
threshold and the attribute is watched against the threshold.

Raised `SweepBudgetSeconds` to 60 and its ceiling to 600. A rate limited
provider gets more of its walk done per chunk and pays the per-chunk
overhead half as often, and `SweepAiringScheduleProviderJob` is capped at
four at a time, so four chunks at the full budget is the worst case.

- Split the threshold lookup out of `JobWatchdog` into
  `JobWatchdogThresholds`, which also owns the `[LongRunning]` exemptions
- Registered `AiringScheduleSweepWatchdogThreshold`, which is 90 seconds
  until the budget passes a minute and `1.5 x` the budget after that
- Documented that shutdown waits for the chunk in flight, so a provider
  ignoring its token holds the server for the rest of its budget

`refactor` (`airing`): **Resolve the sweep watchdog threshold without a cast**:

interface was registered, so the cast was the only way in, and it would have

`fix` (`airing`): **Judge retention on the schedule a write leaves behind**:

Airing retention was enforced in two places that disagreed. `RunRetentionSweep`
removes a schedule only when its *latest* airing has aged out, so a run that
still airs keeps its whole history, while the write path rejected every
individual airing older than the cutoff and failed the submission with it. A
back-catalogue show with a recent episode was refused wholesale even though the
sweep would never have touched it.

`ValidateAirings` no longer looks at slots at all. `WriteAirings` runs the check
once, on the result of the delay inference, which is the schedule exactly as the
write would leave it: the rows it stores, the untouched rows it leaves alone, and
a removal kept as a hiatus, which is still part of the line. `AddOrUpdateAiring`
and `UpdateAiring` judge the stored schedule with the one changed row folded in.
A write is refused only when nothing at all would be left inside the window, and
the rejection is reported under the key `#schedule` rather than an airing's,
since the whole schedule is what would go.

- Matched the slotless arm to the sweep's: a line with no dated airing has no
  date to judge and is kept
- Ran the check before the row is touched on both single-airing paths, so a
  refusal leaves the stored airing as it was
- Documented the rule on `IAiringScheduleService` and in the airing README
- Trimmed the AniList provider's own submission comments to what they do

`fix` (`airing`): **Delete what a `MergeAirings` write names for removal**:

`MergeAirings` and `RemoveAiring` disagreed about what naming an airing
meant. Both are explicit, but only `RemoveAiring` deleted: a named
removal reached the same inference loop a `SetAirings` omission does, so
a future-slotted airing came back as a hiatus and there was no way to
delete one through a delta write at all. `RemoveAiring`'s own doc
already asserted the opposite rule.

The rule is now that explicit removal deletes and absence is a hiatus.
A named removal is deleted whichever side of now its slot is, matching
`RemoveAiring`, and a provider whose removal really is its source
dropping a slot asks for the old judgement with the new
`EpisodeAiringUpdateOptions.KeepRemovalsAsHiatus`.

- Split the removal judgement out of `Infer` into `SplitRemovals`, which
  both the inferring and the store-as-submitted paths run, so the new
  option governs a named removal with `InferDelays` on or off
- Left a `SetAirings` omission alone: it is still a hiatus, and
  `InferDelays = false` still deletes it, since that flag says what a
  literal submission means rather than what a removal does
- Stated the rule on `SetAirings`, `MergeAirings` and `RemoveAiring`,
  and in the airing README
- Added tests for both settings, including the retention interaction: a
  removal kept as a hiatus holds on to the slot it lost and still counts
  towards the window, while a deleted one stops counting

`refactor` (`airing`): **Drop the single-airing writes from the airing contract**:

`IAiringScheduleService` carried `AddOrUpdateAiring`, `UpdateAiring` and
`RemoveAiring` alongside the batch writes, with no caller anywhere: every
provider that exists uses `SetAirings` or `MergeAirings`, and nothing in
`Shoko.Server` or the REST surface reached for them. They were also
divergent, since `AddOrUpdateAiring` hand-rolled its own move detection
against `AiringInferenceOptions.DefaultMoveThreshold`, never inferred
`IsDelayed` and ran no cause detection, so the same airing written through
it and through `MergeAirings` could land as different stored state.

Every single-airing operation is a one-element `MergeAirings` call, which
also gets the inference, so the three are gone rather than kept.

- Removed the three members from the interface and from
  `AiringScheduleService.Airings`
- Removed `EpisodeAiringUpdateData`, the single-airing `ValidateRetention`
  overload and `HasMoved`, which only those paths used
- Kept the batch `ValidateRetention`, `GetOwnedAiring` and `ValidateAirings`,
  which `SetAirings` and `MergeAirings` still need
- Ported the link-head promotion and the retention-on-a-move cases onto
  `MergeAirings`, and dropped the two that `MergeAirings` and `SetAirings`
  already pinned
- Reworked the `README.md` prose and the `<see cref>` links that named them

`feat` (`abstractions`): **Mask configuration secrets on the way out and restore them on the way back**:

Configuration objects carry live credentials and every serializer that
touched them wrote them out in plaintext, so `AniDb.Password`,
`AniDb.AVDumpKey`, `Database.Password` and `TMDB.UserApiKey` reached the
v3 configuration surface and any plugin that serializes a configuration
for a client of its own. `PasswordPropertyTextAttribute` is a
`System.ComponentModel` marker that Newtonsoft ignores entirely, so
nothing was acting on it outside `SettingsProvider.DumpSettings`.

Masking is a property of the transport, not of the model. The model keeps
the truth, so `Load<TConfig>()` still hands a plugin the real
credentials; only serialization for something outside the server masks.

- Added `ConfigurationSecrets` to `Shoko.Abstractions`, a document-level
  masker and restorer keyed off `[PasswordPropertyText]`
- Exposed it through `IConfigurationService` as `SerializeMasked`,
  `MaskSecrets` and `RestoreMaskedSecrets`, so core and plugins share one
  implementation rather than drifting apart
- Made the write path a post-deserialize merge rather than a
  `JsonConverter`, which cannot see the stored value: an absent property
  or the sentinel keeps what is stored, any other value replaces it, and
  an explicit `null` or `""` clears it
- Ran the restore inside `SaveInternal` and `Validate` before any
  validation, so a required secret is never judged on a sentinel
- Rejected the sentinel as a settable value, so nobody is locked out
  without a diagnostic
- Paired collection secrets by the `[Key]` property the schema generator
  already treats as a record's identity, and by the dictionary key for
  dictionaries; a list without one is refused rather than matched by
  position
- Masked the v3 configuration endpoints, `GET /api/v3/Settings`, the
  relocation preset configuration endpoints and both sides of the
  `ConfigurationActionResult` diff
- Added a test over every configuration type that fails when a property
  named like a credential is neither marked nor allowlisted

`fix` (`api`): **Serve the HLS manifest from its session path**:

`Stream/Hls/master.m3u8` returned a manifest whose `init.mp4` and
`segment-{index}.m4s` URIs resolved against `Stream/Hls/`, where no route
exists, so no HLS transform could be played. It now mints the session and
redirects to `Stream/Hls/{sessionID}/master.m3u8`, and `BuildManifest`
carries the request's query string onto every URI so an `apikey` in the
query reaches the segments too. `Stream/Direct` keeps the query string
across its redirect for the same reason.

`feat` (`abstractions`): **Add `IHlsPresentationRendition`**:

Added an HLS rendition shape that serves its own presentation, for output
the core's single-variant, fixed-duration manifest cannot describe:
alternate audio renditions, a bitrate ladder, or segments cut at source
keyframes.

- `OpenResourceAsync` receives every request under
  `Stream/Hls/{sessionID}/`, including `master.m3u8`, with the relative
  path and the query string
- `HlsResource` carries the content type, an optional `ETag`, and the
  position observers are notified with
- `IHlsStreamRendition` and its routes are unchanged

`fix` (`api`): **Mark optional authentication on the stream pipeline routes**:

The `Stream/Transforms`, `Stream/Hls` and `Stream/Direct` routes let
anonymous callers through only when `AllowAnonymousFileStreamingInAPIv3`
is set, like `Stream` itself, but were missing `OptionalAuthentication`,
so the OpenAPI document did not list the API key for them.

`fix` (`streaming`): **Keep a stream session alive while a response is streaming**:

A session's idle time only reset when a request arrived, so a progressive
stream played over one long range request looked idle and was evicted,
with its rendition disposed, under the open response. Streams served from
a session are now wrapped by `StreamSession.Track`, and
`EvictExpiredSessions` skips a session until they are all disposed.
`SessionIdleTimeoutMinutes` now defaults to 10 instead of 3, so a paused
HLS player that has stopped requesting segments survives a longer pause.

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Serve rendition resources for either delivery mode**:

Split the resource half of `IHlsPresentationRendition` into

`fix` (`db`): **Tolerate quoted identifiers when patching stored SQLite DDL**:

comparison and downstream relative-path math. The source-location test
asserts against the folder's platform-normalized path so it holds on
both platforms.

`feat`: **Estimate the air time of episodes AniList has no schedule for**:

AniList's airing schedule gives a precise broadcast time, but only for
the episodes it has scheduled. AniDB has a date for nearly every
episode, including future ones, and already reflects breaks and delays.
The shoko episode now combines the two: when an episode has an AniDB
date but no linked AniList schedule entry, its air time is the AniDB
date, taken as midnight UTC, plus the broadcast time learned from the
series' other linked episodes.

- `AirTimeUtility.LearnAirTimeOffset` takes the median offset over the
  ten most recent aired normal episodes with a known time, so a
  long-running series follows its current slot and a one-off special
  or delay does not skew it; fewer than two samples yields nothing
- `AnimeSeries.AnilistAirTimeOffset` caches the learned offset, reset
  on link and schedule changes and self-healing after an hour
- `AnimeEpisode` applies it in `AirDateWithTime` for normal episodes and
  reports it through the new `IShokoEpisode.IsAirTimeEstimated`
- `IEpisode.AirDate` on the shoko episode is now the UTC calendar day
  of `AirDateWithTime`, so the two never disagree, and a linked series
  takes its days from AniList's broadcast schedule rather than an AniDB
  date that records an early screening
- The AniDB and AniList entities are untouched, and the episode
  matchers keep reading those entities, so estimates never feed matching

`fix` (`core`): **Keep the database blocked after a failed startup**:

`DatabaseUnblockLoop` waited on the blocking tasks with `WaitAny`, which
returns for a faulted task the same as for a completed one, so when
startup failed and the startup task was faulted the loop removed it,
found nothing else blocking, and lifted the block. `IsDatabaseBlocked`
turned false, the `[DatabaseRequired]` acquisition filter let every job
through, and `WaitForDatabaseUnblockedAsync` resolved successfully, all
against repositories that were never loaded. A plugin's recurring sweep
job hit a `NullReferenceException` in `BaseCachedRepository` eight times
this way.

A faulted or cancelled blocking task now keeps the block up and fails
the waiters with the same exception instead.

`fix` (`core`): **Halt the queue for good when startup fails**:

The queue's hosted services are up before the database is, so after a
failed startup the orchestrator kept dispatching whatever the acquisition
filters let through, and a client could resume it through the API or
SignalR at any time. Nothing in a failed process can serve a job.

- Added `Halt` to the orchestrator and `IQueueScheduler`: a pause that
  `Resume` cannot undo for the rest of the process lifetime, with
  `IsHalted` alongside `IsPaused`
- `WorkerPoolManager.Resume` no longer announces a start on a halted queue
- `SystemService` halts the queue when `StartupFailedException` is set

`feat` (`api`): **Put the broadcast time and filters on the calendar episodes**:

`Dashboard.Episode` took its air date straight from the AniDB episode,
so the calendar never saw the times AniList provides or the estimates
the shoko episode derives from them. It now reads the shoko episode
when there is one.

- `AirDate` is the shoko episode's day, the UTC calendar day of the
  broadcast when the time is known
- Added `AiredAt`, the UTC air time, set to midnight on `AirDate` when
  no time is known, with `HasAirTime` and `IsAirTimeEstimated` flags so
  a client can tell a real time from the placeholder
- `CalendarEpisodes` fetches a day either side of the requested range
  and filters on the final day, since a late-night slot can move an
  episode across midnight UTC, and orders by the air time
- Added `includeWithAirTime`, an `IncludeOnlyFilter` on the known
  broadcast time, and a comma-delimited `type` filter on the AniDB
  episode type that defaults to normal episodes
- A series counts as missing when it has no files, not merely when
  Shoko has no entry for it; the series and shoko episode stay attached
  so the card keeps its link and broadcast time
